summary: Register dates the 100-foot Mosinee tower to 1951 and its spring staffing to 2015; City Pages gives other dates, and the ranger station beside it is leased for $1.

facts.design: 100-foot tower with an inside corner ladder

events.note: Register's build year; a City Pages article gives the 1940s for the tower
Register: spring staffing ended when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network

evidence.supports: 100-foot tower with an inside corner ladder
evidence.quote: This 100-foot tower features an inside corner ladder.

evidence.supports: on Ranger Street beside former DNR ranger station; built 1951; staffed to 2015
evidence.quote: Mosinee Tower sits along Ranger Street within the City of Mosinee, adjacent to a former Wisconsin DNR Ranger Station.

evidence.supports: built 1951; staffed intermittently in spring until 2015 when Wisconsin decommissioned its network
evidence.quote: Built in 1951, Mosinee tower was staffed intermittently during spring fire season until 2015 when Wisconsin decommissioned its lookout network.

evidence.quote: The tower was constructed in the 1940s so the DNR could spot forest fires around the area but was decommissioned in the early 2000s

evidence.quote: It was constructed in the 1950s and used as a fire station before being shut down in the mid-90s.

evidence.quote: The Department of Natural Resources says that all 72 towers will be removed from service.

notes_for_editor: Build year is disputed: register says 1951, City Pages says the tower dates from the 1940s. End of service is disputed: register says staffed until 2015, City Pages says decommissioned in the early 2000s; the statewide 2015 announcement fits the register better. The City Pages copy I read is undated and I did not confirm its original outlet. Lease and renovation details come only from City Pages. No public access or climbing source was found. The 1958 photo and register photo credit (WDNR/John Hunt) are already in the record, so no new photos. Two websearch calls were used on this tower.
